title: Prize, Pursue, or Dance Rethinking Some Mindsets to Finding a Spouse
author: Michael Foster
summary: Foster examines the different cultural frameworks through which people approach finding a spouse: the "prize" mentality (viewing spouse as an achievement or status symbol), the "pursuit" mentality (viewing courtship as a hunt or conquest), and the "dance" mentality (viewing courtship as a mutual, reciprocal engagement between two people considering partnership). Foster argues that only the dance mentality produces healthy marriages because it recognizes the other person as a full human being with their own desires, agency, and perspective. The prize mentality turns marriage into self-aggrandizement; the pursuit mentality treats the other as an object to be won. Only the dance mentality creates the mutual respect and genuine regard necessary for long-term partnership.
points: Three cultural frameworks shape how people approach courtship: prize (viewing spouse as achievement), pursuit (viewing as conquest), and dance (viewing as mutual engagement).
The prize mentality turns marriage into self-aggrandizement; the pursuit mentality treats the other as an object to be conquered.
Only the dance mentality produces healthy marriages because it recognizes the other person as a full human being with their own desires, agency, and perspective.
Mutual respect and genuine regard for the other person's humanity and agency are prerequisites for long-term partnership and marital satisfaction.
Cultural mentoring toward mature courtship requires teaching young people to see the other person as they actually are rather than as an achievement, trophy, or object to be won.
